summary: In Greek mythology, Everes or Eueres (Ancient Greek: Εὐήρης, "well-fitted") was a Theban, often described as a shepherd, husband of the nymph Chariclo and father of the blind prophet Tiresias. He is sometimes traced as a descendant of Udaeus, one of the Spartoi sown by Cadmus.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Everes of Thebes was the mortal father, by the nymph Chariclo, of Tiresias. Chariclo is remembered as a favourite attendant of Athena; Everes himself is a genealogical figure whose importance is almost entirely that he anchors Tiresias in the oldest Theban stock.

Ancient and modern notices often make him a descendant of Udaeus, one of the five Spartoi who rose from the dragon's teeth sown by Cadmus when Thebes was founded. That descent places Tiresias among the city's primordial warrior-sown houses.

sections.heading: Role in myth
paragraphs: Everes has no major independent narrative. He appears in mythography as the named father when Apollodorus and others introduce Tiresias (Bibliotheca 3.6.7; Hyginus Fabulae 68, 75). Stories of Tiresias' blinding, sex-change, and long prophetic career belong to the son; Everes remains the Theban shepherd behind that line.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (everes) is the Theban father of Tiresias. Wikipedia's Everes (mythology) also lists an Arcadian son of Heracles and Parthenope, and a Taphian prince who alone survived among the sons of Pterelaus — distinct figures who share only the name.
